title: Automated quantization policy and continuous cosine-drift validation for embeddings
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Goal: Define and implement an automated quantization policy and continuous validation harness for embedding models that combines INT8/FP16 (and experimental FP8) profiles with cosine-similarity drift checks, so we can safely roll quantized variants into production without measurable downstream similarity regressions.

Background: We've seen promising throughput and cost wins from INT8/FP16 quantized embedding variants, but QA has uncovered intermittent cosine-shift regressions on some customer corpora. Current calibration runs are manual nightly jobs and lack an automated gate for canary rollouts. This ticket scopes a production-ready policy + workflow that: (1) generates candidate quant-profiles per-model, (2) runs multi-cohort calibration and accuracy validation, (3) stores signature baselines and anchor cohorts, (4) continuously monitors cosine similarity drift and triggers rollbacks/alerts.

Proposal:
- Quantization profiles: formalize profile objects for INT8/FP16/FP8-experimental that include layer-ignore masks, per-layer scale overrides, and a small set of deterministic RNG seeds for calibration sampling.
- Calibration workflow: build a calibration pipeline that picks N anchors per-corpus (stratified by length and token distribution), runs per-layer calibration sweeps, and produces an acceptance report with unit cost estimates and latency impact. Pipeline will run in k8s Batch and expose metrics to the console.
- Accuracy validation: run embedding similarity comparisons (cosine) across held-out query sets and corpora. Compute distributional metrics (median shift, 95th-percentile degradation, fraction below acceptance threshold). Acceptance criteria default: median cosine shift <= 0.005, 95p shift <= 0.02, and <1% of pairs crossing an application-specific similarity threshold (configurable per-customer workload).
- Drift harness: implement a continuous monitoring job that snapshots baseline signatures weekly, computes cohort-wise cosine divergence, and triggers automated actions: rollback to float variant, open a PagerDuty incident for high-impact customers, or schedule re-calibration.

Acceptance criteria:
1) New quant-profile schema and storage implemented, retrievable via internal API.
2) Automated calibration pipeline produces a human-readable acceptance report and a machine-readable artifact that can be consumed by rollout logic.
3) Validation harness runs on new builds and produces the three metrics above; thresholds are configurable per-project.
4) Continuous drift job runs in prod and emits alerts to the Console + SLI dashboards; documented runbook exists.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- We will default to FP16 for small models where INT8 introduces noticeable outliers; INT8 will be the default profile for large models with extensive calibration anchors.
- FP8 remains experimental and gated behind an opt-in label; we will not auto-roll to FP8 without explicit QA sign-off.
- Calibration sample size tuned to balance compute cost vs false positives; default Nanchors=500 with stratified sampling.

Open questions:
- What SLAs do we apply for the drift monitoring frequency for Dedicated vs Hosted customers? (Triage with GTM/Customer Success).
- Should we persist historical anchor snapshots beyond 90 days or compress them? (Ops input required).

Related artifacts and links: see the attachments field for PRs, runbooks, and dashboards.

Next steps: finish schema and pipeline skeleton (this ticket), then follow-up tickets will implement Console integration and rollout policy automation.
